extracted.intended_audience: wealthy philanthropists, donors, foundation trustees, and those planning large private gifts
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and practices for structuring, selecting, and administering large private gifts and endowments (pensions, public parks, institutional endowments, peace funds) based on Andrew Carnegie's experience and guidance. Covers application systems, beneficiary selection, trustee administration, gift aims, anonymity, and strategic considerations for public benefactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematized application and graduated gift sizing
rubrics_metrics.description: A printed schedule requiring answers to many questions has now to be filled and returned before action is taken. The department is now perfectly systematized and works admirably because we graduate the gift according to the size of the church.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a standardized application process for requests and scale (graduate) gifts to the recipient's size/capacity so distribution is orderly, consistent, and proportionate. Example: Carnegie's organ department required answers via printed schedule and graded gifts by church size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require beneficiary partnership (matching contribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: I decided that I should require a partner in my sin, and therefore asked each congregation to pay one half of the desired new organ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require recipients to contribute (e.g., 50% matching) to ensure buy-in, responsible spending, and that expenditures are needed and reasonable. Carnegie implemented this for organ gifts to prevent waste and to secure congregational commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design gifts to assure needed and reasonable expenditure
rubrics_metrics.description: In requiring the congregation to pay one half the cost of better instruments, there is assurance of needed and reasonable expenditure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure grants so that they incentivize prudent use of funds and avoid unnecessary or excessive projects. Matching requirements and graduated gift scales help secure this outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private pension funds for deserving individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: My private pension fund gives me the highest and noblest return. Modest sums insure this freedom. Not one person have I ever placed upon the pension list that did not fully deserve assistance. It is a real roll of honor and mutual affection. All are worthy. There is no publicity about it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operate private pension programs to provide modest, dignified maintenance for deserving aged beneficiaries. Select beneficiaries carefully (only those 'fully deserve assistance'), keep distributions discreet and without publicity, and prioritize humane outcomes over publicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer personal knowledge in beneficiary selection where feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: Most of the men beneficiaries of the fund I have known personally. They are dear friends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When feasible, select beneficiaries with whom the donor or administrators have personal knowledge or acquaintance to ensure deserving recipients and to preserve donor connection and oversight (as in Carnegie's railroad pension fund).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use endowments with a clear, specific institutional purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The object of the Corporation, as defined by Mr. Carnegie himself in a letter to the trustees, is: 'To promote the advancement and diffusion of knowledge and understanding among the people of the United States by aiding technical schools, institutions of higher learning, libraries, scientific research, hero funds, useful publications and by such other agencies and means as shall from time to time be found appropriate therefor.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating large institutional endowments, define specific charitable objectives in the trust/endowment documents to guide trustees and future administrators. Provide examples of eligible activities and institutions to constrain and focus use of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept major public projects when legitimately requested
rubrics_metrics.description: When Andrew D. White and Mr. Holls ... suggested that I offer the funds needed for a Temple of Peace at The Hague, I informed them that I never could be so presumptuous; that if the Government of the Netherlands informed me of its desire to have such a temple and hoped I would furnish the means, the request would be favorably considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For very large public benefactions, respond to legitimate requests (e.g., from governments or public bodies) rather than acting presumptuously; ensure the recipient institution or government wishes and will properly accept and administer the gift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund institutions that promote public goods like peace and arbitration
rubrics_metrics.description: It created the commanding reality of a permanent tribunal to settle international disputes. ... The day that International Court is established will become one of the most memorable days in the world's history. ... I rejoiced when the Dutch Government made application ... for this Temple of Peace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support organizations and institutions that promote systemic public goods (e.g., international arbitration, peace organizations). Gifts that undergird institutions aimed at preventing large-scale social harms can be prioritized as high-impact philanthropic investments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish trustees and enforceable trust deeds for public gifts
rubrics_metrics.description: Dr. Ross was taken into my confidence so far as Pittencrieff Park was concerned, and with his advice certain men intended for a body of trustees were agreed upon ... and half a million sterling in bonds, bearing five per cent interest, was also to go to them for the benefit of Dunfermline. ... the trustees have succeeded finely in the direction indicated in the trust deed, namely: To bring into the monotonous lives of the toiling masses of Dunfermline, more 'of sweetness and light' ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convey public gifts through a board of trustees and a clear trust deed that states the gift's aims, governance, and an endowment (e.g., income-bearing bonds) for upkeep. Select public-spirited trustees and provide enduring funding for maintenance and activities aligned with the trust's purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design public gifts to uplift the masses—'sweetness and light'
rubrics_metrics.description: To bring into the monotonous lives of the toiling masses of Dunfermline, more 'of sweetness and light,' to give to them--especially the young--some charm, some happiness, some elevating conditions of life ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus community gifts on enhancing quality of life broadly—especially for youth and working classes—by providing access to parks, cultural amenities, and educational opportunities that create lasting social and emotional benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid publicity for certain acts of charity; preserve beneficiaries' privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no publicity about it. No one knows who is embraced. Not a word is ever breathed to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For personal or sensitive distributions (e.g., pensions to individuals), maintain confidentiality and avoid publicizing recipients to protect dignity and prevent solicitation or stigma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select trustees and collaborators of high public spirit and competence
rubrics_metrics.description: They imagined it was in regard to transferring the Park to the town; not even to Dr. Ross was any other subject mentioned. When they heard that half a million sterling ... was also to go to them for the benefit of Dunfermline, they were surprised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose trustees and local collaborators who are public-spirited, competent, and trusted by the community to manage gifts faithfully. Private consultation and careful selection prevent mismanagement and ensure local ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support cultural and social bonding initiatives among beneficiaries
rubrics_metrics.description: The most soothing influence of all was their prompt organization of the Carnegie Veteran Association ... Our yearly dinner together, in our own home in New York, is a source of the greatest pleasure ... Another yearly event ... is our Literary Dinner ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philanthropic programs can include non-monetary supports—events, associations, and ceremonies—that build community, honor service, and sustain relationships between donors and beneficiaries over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider moral and social consequences of gifts and avoid creating dependency
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges were made ... that I was demoralizing Christian worship by giving organs to churches. ... In requiring the congregation to pay one half of the desired new organ ... there is assurance of needed and reasonable expenditure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate social critiques and unintended consequences of gifts; design programs (e.g., matching contributions, conditions) to reduce dependency, promote responsibility, and preserve the recipient institution's integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time philanthropy after accumulation phase; give when able to distribute
rubrics_metrics.description: It is now thirteen years since I ceased to accumulate wealth and began to distribute it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a clear personal timetable: accumulate while productive, then shift to active distribution and stewardship at an appropriate stage in life to ensure effective philanthropic impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund a broad range of public-benefit institutions and causes
rubrics_metrics.description: To aid technical schools, institutions of higher learning, libraries, scientific research, hero funds, useful publications and by such other agencies and means as shall from time to time be found appropriate therefor. ... He gave to the Church Peace Union ... United Engineering Society ... International Bureau of American Republics ... libraries ... research, hospital, and educational boards ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversify philanthropic support across education, libraries, scientific research, peace organizations, professional societies, hospitals, and other public-benefit entities. Record specific beneficiary categories in founding documents to guide long-term use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use social engagement and direct contact as a non-monetary peace-making technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Moral: If you wish to play peace-maker, seat adversaries next each other where they must begin by being civil. ... Most quarrels become acute from the parties not seeing and communicating with each other ... Wise is he who offers the hand of reconciliation ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complement monetary gifts with initiatives that foster direct human contact and reconciliation (e.g., convenings, dinners) to resolve disputes and build mutual understanding—an approach Carnegie used in social peacemaking.
